name: Sternoclavicular Joint Septic Arthritis
definition: Infection of the sternoclavicular joint, potentially dangerous because of proximity to mediastinal structures.

investigations.principle: Blood cultures, inflammatory markers and CT/MRI assess joint and mediastinal extension.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, postoperative, infection, occult injury or condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific pathway.

amber: Abscess or extension may require drainage/debridement.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Sandhi-Shotha framework is secondary to infection treatment.

patientEducation.summary: Infection of the sternoclavicular joint, potentially dangerous because of proximity to mediastinal structures.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, major trauma, unstable fracture/dislocation, sepsis/infection or other listed red flags.
